diagnosis.root_cause: shop-web stopped answering its health probe on http://localhost:8000/health after 09:31:21 while its uvicorn process stayed alive and idle, so Docker marked it unhealthy at 09:32:00. The cause of the stall is not settled: it could be a hang in shop-web's own code or a wait on shop-db, and no collected evidence tells them apart.

evidence.detail: shop-web health probe (urllib to localhost:8000/health, 3s timeout) succeeded once at 09:31:21, then timed out at 09:31:31, 09:31:44 and 09:31:57, with exit 1 each time.
shop-web logged startup complete and 200 responses to /health and /api/items, with no error lines after startup. The timed-out probes left no request line.
shop-web showed CPU 0.0%, memory 57.6 MiB, 4 pids and no block I/O, so the process was alive and idle rather than busy or out of memory.
shop-web has OOMKilled false, restart count 0, restart policy unless-stopped and no mem limit, so no kill or restart occurred.
shop-web became healthy at 09:30:38 and unhealthy at 09:32:00, with no container stop or restart event between them.
shop-db started cleanly at 09:31:10 and is healthy, with no database error shown after that. shop-worker ran its batches without errors.
Repo docs say shop-web connects to shop-db at startup and on every request, so a database wait is one possible cause of the stall.

proposal.reason: I am not sure of the cause: shop-web stopped answering its health probe while its process stayed alive and idle, and the evidence does not separate a hang in its own code from a wait on shop-db. A restart of shop-web alone is the smallest reversible step, leaves shop-db untouched, and tests whether the stall clears; shop-proxy only depends on shop-web and is checked afterwards rather than restarted.

judge_reason: The diagnosis names the right component and the right failure mode. It says shop-web's uvicorn process stayed alive and idle (CPU 0.0%, 4 pids, no OOM kill, no restarts) but stopped answering requests. As a result, the /health probes timed out at 09:31:31, 09:31:44 and 09:31:57, and Docker marked the container unhealthy at 09:32:00. That matches the expected cause: shop-web hangs, the container runs but answers no request, and its health check times out. The evidence is detailed and accurate, including that the timed-out probes left no request line in the logs. The main weakness is that it does not commit to why it stalls. It offers a hang in shop-web's own code and a wait on shop-db as equal possibilities and sets the category to 'unknown'. That leaves open a database cause that the expected output does not support, so it falls short of a clean, committed match.
